name: Joseph Smith Sr.
role: First Presiding Patriarch of the church and one of the Eight Witnesses

name: Lucy Mack Smith
role: Mother of Joseph Smith and author of a foundational family history of the movement

name: Martin Harris
role: One of the Three Witnesses and financier of the Book of Mormon's first printing

name: Alpheus Cutler
role: Founder and first president of the Church of Jesus Christ (Cutlerite)

name: Frederick G. Williams
role: Physician and Second Counselor in the First Presidency (1833-1837)

name: William W. Phelps
role: Early church printer, hymn writer, and scribe; published the Book of Commandments

died.note: Death date disputed: Wikipedia's infobox gives 17 March 1872, but its lead, the Joseph Smith Papers, and the Deseret News obituary (13 March 1872) support 7 March 1872

name: William Marks
role: Nauvoo stake president; later first counselor in the RLDS First Presidency

name: Sidney Rigdon
role: First Counselor in the First Presidency; led a separate faction after 1844 from which the Bickertonite church descends

name: Edward Partridge
role: First bishop of the church

name: Lyman Wight
role: Early Latter Day Saint apostle who led an independent colony in Texas after the 1844 succession crisis

died.note: Date is agreed; place differs by source — Wikipedia says Mountain Valley, Texas; Joseph Smith Papers says Dexter, Medina County, Texas, en route to Missouri.

name: Hyrum Smith
role: Assistant President and Presiding Patriarch of the church and one of the Eight Witnesses

name: Brigham Young
role: Second President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

name: Heber C. Kimball
role: Original member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and First Counselor in the LDS First Presidency

name: John Whitmer
role: First Church Historian and one of the Eight Witnesses

name: Eliza R. Snow
role: Poet and second general president of the LDS Relief Society

name: Willard Richards
role: Apostle, Church Historian, and Second Counselor in the First Presidency of the LDS Church

name: Emma Hale Smith
role: First president of the Female Relief Society of Nauvoo and wife of Joseph Smith

name: David Whitmer
role: One of the Three Witnesses and the last surviving witness of the Book of Mormon

name: Joseph Smith Jr.
role: Founder of the Latter Day Saint movement and publisher of the Book of Mormon

name: Oliver Cowdery
role: Second Elder of the church, principal scribe of the Book of Mormon, and one of the Three Witnesses

name: Wilford Woodruff
role: Fourth President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

born.note: Born in the part of Farmington, Connecticut, that later became Avon; Joseph Smith Papers lists Farmington

name: Parley P. Pratt
role: Original member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and early Latter Day Saint missionary and writer

died.note: Killed in Crawford County, Arkansas; sources place the site near Alma (Wikipedia) or near Van Buren (Joseph Smith Papers)

name: Samuel H. Smith
role: One of the Eight Witnesses and one of the movement's first missionaries

name: John Taylor
role: Third President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

name: William Smith
role: Member of the original Quorum of the Twelve Apostles; later affiliated with the Strangite and RLDS churches

name: Orson Pratt
role: Original member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and leading LDS theologian and mathematician

name: James J. Strang
role: Founder and prophet of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints (Strangite)

died.note: Wikipedia gives 9 July 1856; the Joseph Smith Papers biography gives ca. 26 June 1856 (shot at Beaver Island 16 June, died at Voree).

name: Lorenzo Snow
role: Fifth President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

name: William Clayton
role: Clerk and scribe to Joseph Smith and hymn writer ("Come, Come, Ye Saints")

name: Granville Hedrick
role: Founder and first leader of the Church of Christ (Temple Lot)

born.note: Wikipedia gives the date but no birthplace; Clark County (Clark City), Indiana per Addams & Baugh; date matches his grave marker.

died.note: Wikipedia says he died at Independence, Missouri; Addams & Baugh state he resided in Johnson County, Kansas, until his death. Buried at Hedrick Cemetery, Independence.

sources.label: Addams & Baugh, Beginnings of the Church of Christ (Temple Lot)

name: William Bickerton
role: Founder and first president of The Church of Jesus Christ (Bickertonite)

name: Benjamin F. Johnson
role: 19th-century Latter-day Saint, associate and private secretary of Joseph Smith; the LeBaron branch later claimed its priesthood descends from him

name: John W. Woolley
role: Early Mormon fundamentalist leader regarded by most fundamentalist groups as president of the priesthood

name: Joseph Smith III
role: First Prophet-President of the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints

name: Joseph F. Smith
role: Sixth President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

name: Lorin C. Woolley
role: Mormon fundamentalist leader whose 1886 accounts underpin most fundamentalist priesthood claims; Senior Member of the Priesthood Council (1928-1934)

name: Heber J. Grant
role: Seventh President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

name: Joseph W. Musser
role: Mormon fundamentalist leader and publisher of Truth magazine; Senior Member of the Priesthood Council (1949-1954)

name: Frederick Madison Smith
role: Prophet-President of the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints (1915-1946)

name: John Y. Barlow
role: Mormon fundamentalist leader of the Short Creek community; Senior Member of the Priesthood Council (1935-1949)

name: Alma Dayer LeBaron Sr.
role: Grandson of Benjamin F. Johnson; Mormon fundamentalist excommunicated for plural marriage who claimed the priesthood succession his sons' churches invoke

born.note: Exact birthplace not confirmed in consulted sources; raised partly in Colonia Juárez, Chihuahua, Mexico

name: Leroy S. Johnson
role: Senior Member of the Priesthood Council and prophet of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (1954-1986)

name: Rulon C. Allred
role: Founder and president of the Apostolic United Brethren, a Mormon fundamentalist group (1954-1977)

name: Ross Wesley LeBaron
role: Son of Alma Dayer LeBaron Sr.; co-founder of the Church of the Firstborn of the Fulness of Times who broke away to lead his own Church of the Firstborn

name: Joel LeBaron
role: Son of Alma Dayer LeBaron Sr.; founder and first president of the Church of the Firstborn of the Fulness of Times; murdered on his brother Ervil's orders

name: Ervil LeBaron
role: Son of Alma Dayer LeBaron Sr.; broke from Joel to found the Church of the First Born of the Lamb of God and ordered numerous killings under a blood-atonement doctrine

name: Verlan LeBaron
role: Son of Alma Dayer LeBaron Sr.; succeeded Joel as president of the Church of the Firstborn of the Fulness of Times and was a target of Ervil's faction

died.note: Died in an automobile accident about a day after Ervil; sources give the date as August 16 or August 18, 1981

name: Adam
role: First man in the biblical creation account and progenitor of humankind.

born.note: Traditional Ussher chronology dates Adam's creation to 4004 BC; critical scholarship reads Genesis 1–11 as etiological myth rather than history.

died.note: Genesis 5:5 gives Adam 930 years (Ussher: d. 3074 BC); scholars treat the figure as non-historical.

name: Eve
role: First woman in the biblical creation account, called 'the mother of all living.'

born.note: Traditionally created in the same era as Adam (~4004 BC); critical scholarship reads her as an etiological figure, not historical.

died.note: Scripture records no death date for Eve; this is a traditional estimate near Adam's era, and scholars treat the account as non-historical.

name: Enoch
role: Antediluvian patriarch, son of Jared, who 'walked with God and was taken.'

born.note: Traditional Ussher-based chronology places Enoch's birth ~3382 BC; critical scholarship reads the antediluvian patriarchs as non-historical.

died.note: Enoch was translated, not recorded as dying: Genesis 5:23 gives him 365 years (Heb. 11:5, 'translated that he should not see death'), and LDS scripture (Moses 7) describes Zion taken up to God; traditional translation year ~3017 BC.

name: Noah
role: Patriarch who built the ark and survived the Flood (traditionally 2348 BC).

born.note: Traditional Ussher chronology dates Noah 2948–1998 BC, with the Flood at 2348 BC; scholars view the account as derived from earlier Mesopotamian flood myth.

died.note: Genesis 9:29 gives Noah 950 years (Ussher: d. 1998 BC); critical scholarship treats the figure as non-historical.

name: Abraham
role: Biblical patriarch, called from Ur to Canaan and regarded as the founding father of the covenant lineage.

born.note: Traditional birthplace per Genesis; Ussher-style chronology places his departure from Haran for Canaan c. 1922 BC.

died.place: Cave of Machpelah, near Hebron, Canaan
died.note: Died at 175 and buried at Machpelah per Genesis; critical scholarship views the patriarchal narratives as later literary constructs.

name: Sarah
role: Wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, regarded as a matriarch of the covenant lineage.

born.note: Originally named Sarai; birthplace follows the traditional Genesis account.

died.note: Died at 127 (Gen 23:1) and buried at Machpelah; critical scholarship views the patriarchal narratives as later literary constructs.

name: Isaac
role: Son of Abraham and Sarah and father of Jacob, second of the biblical patriarchs.

born.note: Born to Abraham and Sarah in the land of Canaan per the traditional Genesis account.

died.note: Died at 180 and buried by his sons at Hebron per Genesis; critical scholarship views the patriarchal narratives as later literary constructs.

name: Jacob
role: Son of Isaac, renamed Israel, whose twelve sons are traditionally the ancestors of the tribes of Israel.

born.note: Born in Canaan to Isaac and Rebecca as the second of twins per the traditional Genesis account.

died.note: Died in Egypt at 147 and buried in the Cave of Machpelah at Hebron per Genesis; critical scholarship views the patriarchal narratives as later literary constructs.

name: Joseph (son of Jacob)
role: Son of Jacob who was sold into Egypt and rose to authority under Pharaoh, according to the Genesis account.

born.note: Born to Jacob and Rachel in Paddan Aram per the traditional Genesis account; sold into Egypt c. 1700 BC.

died.note: Died in Egypt at 110, asking that his bones be carried out of Egypt per Genesis; critical scholarship treats the narrative as a later literary composition.

name: Moses
role: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt and received the law at Sinai

born.note: Traditional biblical chronology places his birth ~1526 BC, 80 years before the Exodus (early/biblical date 1446 BC); most scholars regard Moses as a legendary figure and dispute the Exodus's date and historicity.

died.note: Deuteronomy 34:5-6 records his death on Mount Nebo at age 120, but LDS scripture (Alma 45:19) and the Bible Dictionary hold he was translated rather than dying.

name: Aaron
role: Elder brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel

born.note: Traditional chronology places his birth ~1529 BC, three years before Moses; information about Aaron comes only from religious texts.

died.note: Numbers 33:38-39 records his death on Mount Hor at age 123 in the fortieth year after the Exodus; Deuteronomy 10:6 instead names Moserah.

name: Joshua
role: Successor of Moses who led Israel in the conquest of Canaan

born.note: Traditional chronology places his birth ~1500 BC; biblical chronology sets his life in the Bronze Age, with no precise date established by mainstream scholarship.

died.note: Joshua 24:29-30 records his death at age 110 and burial at Timnath-serah (Timnath-heres) in the hill country of Ephraim.

name: David
role: Second king of Israel who established his capital at Jerusalem

born.note: Son of Jesse the Bethlehemite; traditional chronology places his birth ~1040 BC, though the timeframe of his reign is disputed among scholars.

died.note: Traditional chronology has him die ~970 BC at about age 70 after a 40-year reign (~1010-970 BC), ruling from Jerusalem.

name: Solomon
role: Third king of Israel who built the first temple in Jerusalem

born.note: Son of David and Bathsheba; traditional chronology places his birth ~990 BC, with dates described by scholars as hypothesised from biblical chronology.

died.note: Traditional chronology has him die ~931 BC after a 40-year reign (~970-931 BC); his death and the division of the kingdom are dated to 931 BC.

name: Elijah
role: Prophet in the northern kingdom of Israel during the reign of King Ahab (9th century BC).

born.note: Birth year not recorded; estimated from period of activity. Scripture introduces him only as 'the Tishbite.'

died.place: near the Jordan River, by Jericho
died.note: 2 Kings 2 records he was taken up alive in a whirlwind (translated, not recorded as dying); year estimated from his mid-9th-century activity.

name: Isaiah
role: Prophet in the kingdom of Judah whose oracles form the Book of Isaiah.

born.note: Birth year not recorded; estimated from period of activity (prophesied c. 740–686 BC under Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah).

died.note: Death year not recorded; estimated from period of activity. Talmudic tradition holds he was martyred (sawn in two) under Manasseh; time and manner of death are not stated in the Hebrew Bible.

name: Jeremiah
role: Prophet of Judah active from the reign of Josiah through the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem.

born.place: Anathoth, in the territory of Benjamin
born.note: Birth year not recorded; estimated from period of activity (called as a prophet in 626 BC, the 13th year of Josiah).

died.note: Death year not recorded; estimated from period of activity. Taken to Egypt after Jerusalem's fall (587 BC); no authentic record of his death survives.

name: Daniel
role: Jewish exile in Babylon and namesake of the Book of Daniel.

born.note: Birth year not recorded; estimated from period of activity. A noble Judahite youth carried to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar (traditionally 605 BC).

died.note: Death year not recorded; estimated from period of activity — last dated reference is the third year of Cyrus; burial site is disputed by tradition.

name: Josiah
role: King of Judah (reigned 640–609 BC), known for his religious reforms.

born.note: Born c. 648 BC; became king at age eight in 640 BC (2 Kings 22).

died.note: Fatally wounded fighting Pharaoh Necho II at Megiddo in 609 BC; accounts differ on whether he died there (2 Kings) or after being carried to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles).

name: Jesus Christ
role: Central figure of Christianity, believed by Christians to be the Son of God and the Messiah

born.note: Scholars place his birth roughly 6–4 BC; the traditional December 25 date is not historically certain.

died.note: Crucified under Pontius Pilate; Christian and LDS belief holds that he rose from the dead (the Resurrection).

name: John the Baptist
role: Jewish prophet who baptized Jesus and preached repentance in the region of the Jordan

born.note: Traditionally a kinsman of Jesus, born shortly before him.

died.note: Beheaded on the order of Herod Antipas after rebuking his marriage to Herodias.

name: Peter the Apostle
role: Chief of the Twelve Apostles and a leading figure of the early Christian church

born.note: A Galilean fisherman, originally named Simon, called by Jesus to be an apostle.

died.note: Church tradition holds he was martyred by crucifixion in Rome under Nero, sometime between about AD 64 and 68.

name: Paul the Apostle
role: Apostle to the Gentiles and author of numerous epistles in the New Testament

born.note: Born a Jew and Roman citizen; originally named Saul before his conversion.

died.note: Church tradition holds he was martyred in Rome under Nero, sometime around AD 64–67.

name: Jared
role: Jaredite patriarch who led his family from the Tower of Babel to a promised land in the Americas.

born.place: Mesopotamia, near the great tower (Tower of Babel)
born.note: The Book of Mormon gives no birth year; this is an approximation from the Jaredite departure tied to the Tower of Babel (~2200 BC).

died.note: The Book of Mormon gives no death year; this is an approximation from the Jaredite era after the ocean crossing to the promised land.

name: Brother of Jared (Mahonri Moriancumer)
role: Unnamed Jaredite prophet whose faith preserved his people's language at the Tower of Babel; Joseph Smith is traditionally reported to have given his name as Mahonri Moriancumer.

born.place: Mesopotamia, near the great tower (Tower of Babel)
born.note: The Book of Mormon gives no birth year; this is an approximation from the Jaredite departure tied to the Tower of Babel (~2200 BC). He is unnamed in the text.

died.note: The Book of Mormon gives no death year; this is an approximation from the Jaredite era after the ocean crossing to the promised land.

name: Lehi
role: Prophet who led his family out of Jerusalem about 600 BC and across the ocean to a promised land.

born.place: Jerusalem or its vicinity, Kingdom of Judah
born.note: The Book of Mormon gives no birth year; this is an approximation from his being an established prophet who left Jerusalem about 600 BC.

died.note: The Book of Mormon gives no death year; this is an approximation within the 2 Nephi 4 span (about 588–570 BC), where the record states Lehi 'waxed old' and 'died, and was buried.'

name: Nephi (son of Lehi)
role: Son of Lehi, prophet and record-keeper who led his people after their arrival in the promised land.

born.note: The Book of Mormon gives no birth year; this is an approximation from his being a young man when the family left Jerusalem about 600 BC.

died.note: The Book of Mormon gives no death year; this is an approximation from the Jacob 1 span (about 544–421 BC), which opens with the record 'Nephi died.'
